output: {"objective":"Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of JAK3-p.Arg103His (JAK3, UniProt P52333) and test it with one targeted computational test.","subject":{"gene":"JAK3","variant_id":"JAK3-p.Arg103His","accession":"P52333","position":103,"reference_residue":"R","alternate_residue":"H","protein_change":"p.Arg103His"},"events":51,"current_favourite":"H1","hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":1,"statement":"R103H is a buried-core substitution in the JAK3 FERM domain. Replacing arginine with histidine removes a side-chain interaction that holds the FERM fold together, so the protein is destabilised or misfolded and degraded, which lowers JAK3 levels and signalling.","supports":["E4","E7","E12","E14","E15","E16","E18","E1","E10"],"would_refute":"An AlphaFold model or experimental model shows R103 side chain solvent-exposed (relative SASA above about 25%) with no polar or salt-bridge partner, and a stability predictor (e.g. FoldX or Rosetta ddG) gives |ddG| below 1 kcal/mol for R103H.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"protein_interaction","starting_rank":2,"statement":"R103H folds normally but removes a surface contact that JAK3 needs to couple to the common gamma chain (IL2RG) or other cytokine receptors through its N-terminal FERM region, so receptor association and STAT activation fail.","supports":["E5","E20","E10","E19","E13"],"would_refute":"In a predicted JAK3 complex with the gamma chain or a cytokine receptor intracellular region (e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer or a docking model), R103 lies more than 10 Å from any receptor residue, and its buried surface area does not change between wild type and R103H.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"domain_interface","starting_rank":3,"statement":"R103H sits at an intramolecular FERM-SH2 or FERM-kinase interface. Losing the arginine breaks the autoinhibitory or scaffold contact that positions the kinase domain, so catalytic output is reduced.","supports":["E8","E4","E7","E11"],"would_refute":"In the AlphaFold model, R103 has no atom within 5 Å of any SH2 or kinase-domain residue, and the FERM-SH2 and FERM-kinase interface contacts are unchanged when R103H is modelled, so the residue sits outside the inter-domain interface.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"results":[{"test_id":"T1","test_kind":"stability_effect","summary":"FoldX predicted ΔΔG for R103H on the AlphaFold model AF-P52333-F1 is +4.15 kcal/mol, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold (ProtVar display bins). Control: local pLDDT at residue 103 is 95.88, so the model confidence supports interpretation. Within-site control: R103C at the same residue gives ΔΔG +2.02 kcal/mol.","headline":"FoldX predicts ΔΔG +4.15 kcal/mol for R103H, at or above the destabilising threshold of 2.0 kcal/mol.","verdict":"predicted_destabilising","job_id":null}]}
